[quote=tallisland;60636797][Spoiler=Red July, Maroon August] 

The cyber attacks headed by the Thýven Republicans against the Tallislandic government proved effective in halting some government actions, though the attack also had many negative side effects.

In response to the Internet downings, the State of Rechia sent phonecalls to local police offices demanding state curfews for all citizens by 8 P.M, with orders to arrest anyone seen after hours. This proved effective in allowing law enforcement to end protests in Braanikov and Morawik, though this only enraged protestors in Tremilov.

As a result, the Tremilov protestors were able to push law enforcement out of the city entirely, planning to use the Rechia State Highway to link up and unite with Zelenovik. Following the seizure of Tremilov, the Governor of Rechia declared martial law mere days after the declaration of a curfew, deploying the Tallislandic national guard to restore control in all cities affected by the coalition's rise.

 

Jastrzeburg in the Eyjafjollum region was quickly seized by the coalition protestors, thanks mostly to the withdrawal of Government forces from the region to prevent equipment falling into the hands of the coalition. The seizure of Jastrzeburg however allowed for protestors in Dabrichau and Zielenstadt to unite into one unit. 

Following their unification, Kjersti Stennes made a public declaration online that the Anti-Principalist Coalition was the rightful government of Tallisland, that the government of Clifford Prisk was corrupt and had illegally skewed the earlier 2026 elections to prevent her Radicalist victory.

The Tallislandic government would usually be able to suppress these posts very quickly, but was unable to rally a significant resistance online as the post spread like wildfire and gathered support across the country. The words of Stennes emboldened resistance on the Grimsdalr Peninsula, with most government forces retreating to protect Hoscbus and Jaerlic.

Subsequently, Lukylod, Ofenhind, Miswig, Gliwig, Karwbridc, and Ironlorkston all fell to the Coalition, their police stations and armories raided and used to arm protestors. Rebel sentiment would only increase more as the Internet downing persisted.

When the Tallislandic government did eventually fix it's security issues, taking advice from Neue Republik advisors with prior knowledge on cybersecurity from the Nestor-Sikirsk conflict.

With all of this considered, Holy President Prisk followed the lead of Rechia and declared nationwide martial law. Where local law enforcement held control, citizens were to be corralled out of the streets into their homes, with those that refuse to be arrested.

To cities where the coalition had taken control, an ultimatum was issued on national television: Turn yourselves in within five days, or face the Tallislandic military.

Units were activated nationwide, rallying at Mirkówka, Byster, Jaerlic, Osliburne, and Evraibal, deploying all 100,000 active personnel across these locations, with 30,000 national guard scattered across the country. Holy President Prisk would also attempt to get into contact with the AWN, to which he was consistently unable to, worryingly.

Prisk was realizing far too late that the corporations were not on his side despite their silence, and like the greedy demons they are, they were merely waiting for their chance to show their true colors. After all, it takes a snake like Prisk to identify the other snakes around him.

In the meantime, Finley Gallagher continued his futile attempts at calling for the end of aggression, for both sides to lay down their weapons and negotiate an end.

Nobody ever listens to a centrist, however.[/spoiler][/quote]
[spoiler=Meeting in Shiganuur]
[b][i]5th of September, 2026[/i]
[i]District of Shiganuur, House of White Petals[/i][/b]

The Khatun of Alaqar takes a seat at the far side of a dark-stained table, seating herself next to her Minister of Intelligence and Minister of Foreign Relations respectively. She scans the room around her and is met with focused eyes. She determines that, yes, we are ready to begin.

Well then, gentlemen, it is a pleasure meeting with you all this evening. As you might know, Tallisland is experiencing some internal unrest from within. Im not quite sure what or how the THEP or EDU are going to react to this, considering the Tallislandics are a member of both, but we do have an opportunity for our best interests.

A map of the Shamatine Strait sits squarely in the middle of the table, showing an overhead view of the island of Tel Karmiw. Alaqan military positions on the coast of Issyk were marked with various numbers, badges and lines. General Khongtaghar spoke up first.

Do you have ANY information on what is going on in Tel Karmiw at all? I get that theyre not doing so hot in Elseyr but an invasion of Tel Karmiw when nothing has happened to it may look a little aggressive.
Sorry, but I simply do not believe that aggressive is a good enough argument considering the state that Erene is in right now. Well call it an intervention just to stay internationally safe and then SECURE it from the Lusandric Church to keep them to imposing authoritarianism on the island. Simple.

Hmm well, they cant really make a good argument for imperialism if its a liberation force, but we need to wait for something to actually happen there before we kick anything off.
This I am willing to oblige by. All in favor of an intervention of Tel Karmiw?
Aye.

The cabinet is quietly discussing amongst themselves on what their next course of action is. General Khongtaghar was already drawing up and discussing plans for the intervention in Tel Karmiw. Indeed, he was very much in support of this idea. The Khatuns butler walks in with a cup of tea and a napkin embroidered with silver. The Khatun has a request to make.
Alright then. Subetei?
Yes, my Imperial Khatun?
Could you deliver these orders to the Commanders headquarters? I need these plans to be sent discreetly and without delay. Understood?
Understood.
[/spoiler]

[b]September 10, 2026: The Right of the Peoples[/b]

The actions by the patriarch had failed to quell the protests that had arisen in the cities of Malberg, Droen, and Jassel, as the presence of IDF commanders (colonels) gave further rise to disgruntlement. The primary groups behind the protests were the Peoples Party of North Thýven and the Peoples Front of Malbert, both left-leaning socialist-communist groups which held major political sway in the cities at least in terms of labour. The groups claimed that by calling in a paramilitary group to restore order, the patriarchate and thus the government of Thýven as a whole had violated the second promise of Mendenavism, freedom. Though right in a degree, Patriarch Mendenav attempted to paint the bringing in of the IDF commanders as a ploy to protect freedom.

As September 10th came across Thýven, the two groups began to call for the Patriarch to Grant them the right of the peoples which essentially was a historical saying demanding audience with the government, usually the head of state. However, Mendenav was not willing to risk his position amongst the hardline Mendenavists by being seen as too willing to cooperate with ideologies which were enemies to the ideology. Thus hed appoint the district representative, Piter Drømm, a native of Jassel, and peach farmer, to meet with the groups on behalf of the patriarchate and the government.

While the appointment of a mediator angered the two groups, they were willing to settle with it, permitting Drømm to act as a voice of the Patriarchate, despite his lack of knowledge or expertise in the affairs of the church. 

The meetings began at noon on the 10th, where the primary grievances would be laid out, primarily corruption accusations, though some separatist rhetoric was also displayed as the Peoples Party of North Thýven held the belief that the 2025 reunification of Thýven and North Thýven had been nullified and illegal under the collapse of Elseyr-Vespurias. 

Ending by 5 PM on the 10th, Piter Drømm had managed to get the two groups to agree to two main deals, mainly:

[list]1. The integrity of Thýven and its peoples was paramount above all ideological fronts, and all parties involved must consider that to be the ultimate goal.

2. Corruption within the governments of the three cities would be handled by locally established citizens councils.[/list]

The two deals known as The two points of freedom had unintentionally given the communists and socialists in the region almost free reign in their actions to potentially call for the formation of a separate confederation, though equal in political standing to a principate, akin to the Free Republic of Knygta and Deyn, though, this wasnt to be realised just yet.
